t: Zigzag Level Sum of Binary Tree
o: BFS the tree level by level. Within each level, order nodes left-to-right on odd levels (1-based) and right-to-left on even levels; then walk that order, accumulating values, but stop BEFORE the first node failing its level's child condition (odd level: must have a left child; even level: must have a right child) — the failing node is not counted. Levels contain ALL nodes at that depth, regardless of whether their parents were processed.
k: Collect complete levels with a normal BFS first; the zigzag ordering and truncation are applied per level afterwards.
The stopping check applies to the node itself (its required child), and the failing node contributes nothing.

a.i: Standard BFS records each depth's nodes. For level index li (0-based): traversal order is the level as-is if li is even (level 1, 3, ...), reversed if odd. Scan that order, breaking (without adding) at the first node missing the required child.
s: For each level: choose order (reverse on even 1-based levels).
Accumulate values until a node lacks its required child; append the sum (0 if the first node fails).
a.t: O(n) — each node visited a constant number of times

w: The subtle point is that levels are built from the FULL tree, not only from processed nodes — verify with example 1 where node 1 (child of the unprocessed node 2) still appears at level 3. Use 64-bit accumulation for sums (up to 1e5 nodes * 1e5). Follow-up: return the truncated node lists, or apply the rule with k-ary trees.
